newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: N.Korean defector had family tragedy --newspapers.
newsitem.headline: N.Korean defector had family tragedy --newspapers.

text.p: In another daring defection from North Korea, a man whose family reportedly fell foul of Pyongyang's communist government arrived at Seoul international airport on Sunday.
Kang Chul-ho contacted South Korean authorities while in transit on a flight from Beijing to Osaka, Japan, an intelligence official confirmed on Monday.
He claimed he fled to China from North Korea in October 1992, said the official at the Agency for National Security Planning, who declined to be named.
Media reports said Kang's father was executed in public as an ideological foe of North Korea's Stalinist government, and his mother and sister both committed suicide.
One report in the Chosun Ilbo newspaper said he had spent three-and-a-half years in a political prison camp until 1991.

Last Thursday a North Korean woman in her 20s fled barefoot and hungry to South Korea through the heavily mined and guarded Demilitarised Zone that has bisected the Korean peninsula since the 1950-53 Korean War.
South Korea is negotiating with China, so far unsuccessfully, for safe passage to Seoul of North Korea's top ideologue, who defected to a South Korean diplomatic mission in Beijing on February 12.
Near famine conditions in North Korea, and apparent disaffection among some members of the ruling elite, has prompted a string of defections in recent months.
Adding to an impression of instability, the country's defence minister and his deputy both died in quick succession last month, and the prime minister was replaced.
The domestic Yonhap news agency said Kang, 33, stepped off a Korea Air flight on Sunday and made a request for asylum to Kimpo airport police in the transit lounge.

He was travelling under a fake name using forged Chinese seaman's papers and was on his way to Japan with 11 mainland Chinese and ethnic Korean Chinese seamen to work for a Japanese fishing company, Yonhap said.

"Because my father was executed publicly as an ideological offender and my mother and sister committed suicide, I was disillusioned with the North Korean system," Yonhap quoted Kang as telling investigators.
Kang had recently enrolled at a Chinese sea school after working as a labourer in the country, Yonhap said.
The Chosun Ilbo daily quoted Kang as telling a reporter who contacted him in China that he was forced to denounce his father at his execution.

South Korean authorities have become wary of revealing personal details of North Korean asylum seekers since a high-profile defector, reportedly once related through marriage to North Korean leader Kim Jong-il, was shot by two gunmen in a Seoul suburb on February 15.

Seoul police have said they believed North Korean hitmen were responsible and the assassination was intended as a warning to ideologue Hwang Jang-yop, now holed-up in Seoul's mission in Beijing, and other would-be defectors.
Nevertheless, the Chosun Ilbo published a picture of Kang wearing a smart jacket and thick sweater.
Yonhap quoted an unnamed intelligence official as saying if Kang was confirmed to be a North Korean, South Korea would grant him asylum on humanitarian grounds.
South Korean officials believe there are hundreds, possibly thousands, of North Korean escapees in China and Russia waiting for the chance to flee to Seoul.
